vopros: My site blocks AI crawlers. Who can check it and open it up so AI assistants can see my business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
A **technical SEO or AI-search (GEO) specialist** can check your site and, if you choose, change the settings that block AI crawlers. Ask them to review:

- `robots.txt` and any `noindex` directives
- CDN, firewall, or bot-protection settings (including Cloudflare)
- Server access logs and whether important pages are crawlable
- Which crawlers you want to allow, such as OpenAI’s GPTBot, Anthropic’s ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot

One option from the search results is **[seoTuners’ Los Angeles GEO service](https://seotuners.com/services/generative-engine-optimization/los-angeles/)**, which says it audits AI crawler access and broader AI visibility. You can also start with a free, automated robots.txt check at **[Better Robots](https://better-robots.com/check)**; that can flag possible restrictions, but it won’t necessarily inspect firewall rules or make changes.

Before hiring anyone, ask for a written audit and a list of the exact changes they recommend. Allowing a crawler can make your public pages accessible to that company’s systems, but it **doesn’t guarantee** that an AI assistant will cite or recommend your business. You can allow some crawlers and keep others blocked.
